newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia three-month KLIBOR fixed at 10.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia three-month KLIBOR fixed at 10.3 pct.

text.p: Malaysia's benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) was fixed at 10.3 percent at 0300 GMT.
It was at 11.3 percent on Tuesday.
The one-month KLIBOR was fixed at 11.3 percent against 12.85 percent on Tuesday.
KLIBOR is fixed by taking an average of rates offered by various banks in the country.
Money market dealers said despite the slight drop, rates remained high due to tight market liquidity.
"The market is still short of funds. Bank Negara is lending but only to selected finance and discount houses," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
The liquidity squeeze followed heavy buying of the ringgit by the central bank last week to defend the ringgit from a speculative attack.
Although the actual size of the intervention was not known, dealers have estimated that between 2.5 billion and 5.0 billion ringgit was drained from the system.
Dealers said there was still confusion over where rates were heading.

Malaysia's Acting Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Tuesday the country did not favour a high interest rate regime. But, the central bank was not helping to ease the market, dealers said.
"The ball is in Negara's court. It's a question of when they will pump in funds," said another dealer.
Dealers said maturity of Bank Negara bills worth 500 million ringgit on Wednesday was not expected to have much impact on market liquidity.
One-month money was quoted at 10/12 percent against 9/10 percent on Tuesday.
One-week money was at 11/12 percent, against 13/15 percent.
The overnight rate was expected to remain around 10 percent, dealers said.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were mostly untraded to reflect the uncertainty over the direction of interbank rates.
At 0330 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up one point to 92.38, or an implied yield of 7.62 percent.
